svg.aria-label: Diagram of the Sea compiler targeting the Little Man Stack Machine. A Sea for loop that prints i * i for i < 4 compiles to 27 lines of LMSM stack assembly, each block linked to the source it came from; a program counter then steps through the assembly, showing the stack and accumulator, and the output reads 0 1 4 9.
svg.text: The compiler I wrote for MSU's systems course, emitting stack-machine assembly for a 100-cell teaching computer.
1 · compile: each Sea construct becomes a block of stack code
2 · run: step through it on the LMSM

g.text: CALL jump to main, remembering where to return
SPSUB make room on the stack for local i
SSTA pop, then store into a stack slot (i)
SLDA copy a stack slot (i) onto the top
SCMPLT pop two, push 1 if second < top
SPOP pop the top into the accumulator
BRZ leave the loop if the accumulator is 0
SLDA copy a stack slot (i) onto the top
SLDA copy a stack slot (i) onto the top
SMUL pop two, push their product
SPOP pop the top into the accumulator
SLDA copy a stack slot (i) onto the top
SADD pop two, push their sum
SSTA pop, then store into a stack slot (i)
BRA jump back to the loop test

svg.text: Each Sea construct compiles to a small block of stack code; locals live in stack slots.
Running it: SLDA copies i to the top, SCMPLT tests i < 4, SPOP moves the result to the accumulator …
… and every OUT prints i * i, so the tape reads 0 1 4 9.
